=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly attached at the same node, visible in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at nodes, not spread out along the stem)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade, no divisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth with no visible teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (longer than wide, tapering to a point at apex, broad at base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point, not long and drawn out)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base appears broad and curved, not tapering or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (one central midrib with lateral veins branching off, visible in all images)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, moderately spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, running perpendicular to midrib, spaced at regular intervals)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface has a glossy appearance, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, not elongated, attaching leaf blade directly to stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and rigid, with bark-like texture, consistent with young woody plant)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: greenish-brown (stem is primarily green with brownish patches, possibly due to age or environmental exposure)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels; some minor scarring or discoloration present but not textured)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases in any image)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no milky sap or latex exudate visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base or petiole attachment, not visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils present)

F. Notes: Some leaves show minor damage including small holes and slight edge irregularities, likely from environmental exposure or minor physical disturbance. The seedling is marked with a pink tag, which is not a natural feature. Images show the same individual from multiple angles, confirming whorled leaf arrangement and consistent leaf morphology. No flowers, fruits, or reproductive structures visible.
